rv.q: But as a work of theater, “Dreaming Zenzile” struggles among the competing forms of recital, dream play, memory play and biography.
Yet somewhere in all that collaboration, Somi Kakoma’s bio-musical about the great South African singer Zenzile Miriam Makeba has slipped halfway through the cracks.
Overall, though, this bio-musical is an excellent one that feels fresh amid the many others on Broadway and beyond right now.
Dreaming Zenzile, while assuredly Kakoma’s homage, is also an opportunity to show off her magnificent voice.
As far as jukebox musicals go, Dreaming Zenzile earns a B-: plenty of musical gems decorating a rough book.

cn.t: Somi Kakoma delivers a vocally commanding tribute to Miriam Makeba that critics find inspiring and heartfelt, though some note the production feels unfinished and struggles with acoustics at its downtown venue.
